import React from 'react';

import { useResponsive } from '@actual-app/components/hooks/useResponsive';
import { View } from '@actual-app/components/view';

import { Sidebar } from './Sidebar';
import { useSidebar } from './SidebarProvider';

export function FloatableSidebar() {
  const sidebar = useSidebar();
  const { isNarrowWidth } = useResponsive();

  const sidebarShouldFloat = sidebar.floating;

  return isNarrowWidth ? null : (
    <View
      onMouseOver={
        sidebarShouldFloat
          ? e => {
              e.stopPropagation();
              sidebar.setHoveringSidebar(true);
            }
          : undefined
      }
      onMouseLeave={
        sidebarShouldFloat ? () => sidebar.setHoveringSidebar(false) : undefined
      }
      style={{
        position: sidebarShouldFloat ? 'absolute' : undefined,
        top: 8,
        // If not floating, the -50 takes into account the transform below
        bottom: sidebarShouldFloat ? 8 : -50,
        zIndex: 1001,
        borderRadius: sidebarShouldFloat ? '0 6px 6px 0' : 0,
        overflow: 'hidden',
        boxShadow:
          !sidebarShouldFloat || sidebar.hidden
            ? 'none'
            : '0 15px 30px 0 rgba(0,0,0,0.25), 0 3px 15px 0 rgba(0,0,0,.5)',
        transform: `translateY(${!sidebarShouldFloat ? -8 : 0}px)
                      translateX(${
                        sidebarShouldFloat && sidebar.hidden ? '-100' : '0'
                      }%)`,
        transition:
          'transform .5s, box-shadow .5s, border-radius .5s, bottom .5s',
      }}
    >
      <Sidebar />
    </View>
  );
}

import { useResponsive } from '@actual-app/components/hooks/useResponsive';
import { fireEvent, render } from '@testing-library/react';
import { beforeEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest';
import type { Mock } from 'vitest';

import { useSidebar } from './SidebarProvider';

import { FloatableSidebar } from './index';

vi.mock('@actual-app/components/hooks/useResponsive', () => ({
  useResponsive: vi.fn(),
}));

vi.mock('./SidebarProvider', () => ({
  useSidebar: vi.fn(),
}));

vi.mock('./Sidebar', () => ({
  Sidebar: () => <div data-testid="sidebar-stub" />,
}));

describe('FloatableSidebar', () => {
  let setHoveringSidebar: Mock;

  beforeEach(() => {
    vi.clearAllMocks();
    setHoveringSidebar = vi.fn();
    (useResponsive as unknown as Mock).mockReturnValue({
      isNarrowWidth: false,
    });
  });

  function setup({
    floatingSidebar = true,
    alwaysFloats = false,
  }: { floatingSidebar?: boolean; alwaysFloats?: boolean } = {}) {
    (useSidebar as unknown as Mock).mockReturnValue({
      hidden: false,
      setHidden: vi.fn(),
      setHoveringSidebar,
      floating: floatingSidebar || alwaysFloats,
      alwaysFloats,
    });
    return render(<FloatableSidebar />);
  }

  it('reports hovering the sidebar on mouse over when floating', () => {
    const { getByTestId } = setup({ floatingSidebar: true });

    fireEvent.mouseOver(getByTestId('sidebar-stub').parentElement as Element);

    expect(setHoveringSidebar).toHaveBeenCalledWith(true);
  });

  it('reports the sidebar as no longer hovered on mouse leave when floating', () => {
    const { getByTestId } = setup({ floatingSidebar: true });

    fireEvent.mouseLeave(getByTestId('sidebar-stub').parentElement as Element);

    expect(setHoveringSidebar).toHaveBeenCalledWith(false);
  });

  it('does not attach hover handlers when the sidebar is docked (not floating)', () => {
    const { getByTestId } = setup({
      floatingSidebar: false,
      alwaysFloats: false,
    });
    const wrapper = getByTestId('sidebar-stub').parentElement as Element;

    fireEvent.mouseOver(wrapper);
    fireEvent.mouseLeave(wrapper);

    expect(setHoveringSidebar).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
  });
});

// @ts-strict-ignore
import React, {
  createContext,
  useContext,
  useEffect,
  useLayoutEffect,
  useMemo,
  useState,
} from 'react';
import type { Dispatch, ReactNode, SetStateAction } from 'react';

import { useResponsive } from '@actual-app/components/hooks/useResponsive';

import { closeContextMenu } from '#contextmenu/contextMenuSlice';
import { useGlobalPref } from '#hooks/useGlobalPref';
import { useDispatch } from '#redux';

const HOVER_HIDE_DELAY = 350;

type SidebarContextValue = {
  hidden: boolean;
  setHidden: Dispatch<SetStateAction<boolean>>;
  setHoveringSidebar: Dispatch<SetStateAction<boolean>>;
  floating: boolean;
  alwaysFloats: boolean;
};

const SidebarContext = createContext<SidebarContextValue>(null);

type SidebarProviderProps = {
  children: ReactNode;
};

export function SidebarProvider({ children }: SidebarProviderProps) {
  const [floatingSidebar] = useGlobalPref('floatingSidebar');
  const [hidden, setHidden] = useState(true);
  const { width } = useResponsive();
  const alwaysFloats = width < 668;
  const floating = floatingSidebar || alwaysFloats;
  const dispatch = useDispatch();

  // A dropdown menu opened from the sidebar (e.g. BudgetName's) renders in a
  // portal, outside the sidebar's own DOM subtree, so hovering it never
  // triggers the sidebar's onMouseOver/onMouseLeave. Track hover of the
  // sidebar and of any open popover separately, then derive `hidden` from
  // both combined, so the sidebar (and its menu) stay visible while either
  // is being used, and only hide together once neither is hovered anymore.
  const [hoveringSidebar, setHoveringSidebar] = useState(false);
  const [hoveringPopover, setHoveringPopover] = useState(false);

  useEffect(() => {
    function handlePointerOver(e: PointerEvent) {
      const target = e.target as Element | null;
      setHoveringPopover(!!target?.closest?.('[data-popover]'));
    }
    document.addEventListener('pointerover', handlePointerOver);
    return () => document.removeEventListener('pointerover', handlePointerOver);
  }, []);

  useLayoutEffect(() => {
    if (hoveringSidebar || hoveringPopover) {
      setHidden(false);
      return;
    }
    const timeout = setTimeout(() => setHidden(true), HOVER_HIDE_DELAY);
    return () => clearTimeout(timeout);
  }, [hoveringSidebar, hoveringPopover]);

  useEffect(() => {
    if (hidden && !hoveringPopover) {
      dispatch(closeContextMenu());
    }
  }, [hidden, hoveringPopover, dispatch]);

  return (
    <SidebarContext.Provider
      value={{ hidden, setHidden, setHoveringSidebar, floating, alwaysFloats }}
    >
      {children}
    </SidebarContext.Provider>
  );
}

export function useSidebar() {
  const { hidden, setHidden, setHoveringSidebar, floating, alwaysFloats } =
    useContext(SidebarContext);

  return useMemo(
    () => ({ hidden, setHidden, setHoveringSidebar, floating, alwaysFloats }),
    [hidden, setHidden, setHoveringSidebar, floating, alwaysFloats],
  );
}

797:Issue #68 asks for an audit of how the side panel (the left `Sidebar`) and the main budget view are laid out, so that both share one layout context and the main content can react to whether the panel is open. Issue #69 builds on this to resize the main content. **Taking the floating sidebar out of `position: absolute` is deferred to #69**, because doing it here causes a regression. That leaves #68 as a small change: write up the audit, and give the layout one source of truth for the panel's state.

815:**Out of scope (leave untouched):** the main content's `width: '100%'` and any use of `useSidebar` in `FinancesApp` (both belong to #69). # GitHub Issue #68 Summary

**Title:** "Audit layout structure and refactor side panel into the layout flow"

**Repository:** CSCI-435-SE/actual-budget

**Status:** Open

**Assignee:** jamesleonard3rd

**Label:** scope: medium

**Milestone:** Sprint 1

## Issue Body

**Summary:**
The issue requests an audit of the current positioning method for the side panel and main budget view, followed by restructuring to place both elements within a shared layout context (flexbox or grid) rather than having the panel overlay the content. The goal is to establish the structural foundation without implementing resizing behavior at this stage.

**User Story:**
"As a developer, I want the side panel and main content to share a common layout container so that the main content can respond to the panel's open state."

**Tasks:**
- Document the panel's current positioning approach and main layout composition
- Integrate the panel and main content into a unified flex/grid container
- Eliminate or modify absolute/fixed positioning that removes the panel from the document flow
- Make the panel's open/closed state accessible to the layout system

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Panel and main content operate within the same layout context
- Panel open/close functionality remains unchanged with no style modifications
- No impact to existing navigation or budget features
- Audit findings documented in the issue or associated pull request

**Note:** No comments or activity recorded beyond the initial issue creation.

# GitHub Issue #69 Summary

**Title:** "Resize main content when side panel is open or closed"

**Full Issue Body:**

**Summary:**
Using the new layout structure, make the main content area reflow to fill only the remaining space when the panel is open, and return to its original width when the panel closes.

**User Story:**
"As a user who opens the side panel while reviewing my budget, I want the main content to resize alongside it so that nothing is hidden behind the panel."

**Tasks:**
- Bind the main content's width or offset to the panel's open state
- Ensure the content reflows (no fixed widths that force it to render at full width beneath the panel)
- Restore the original layout and width when the panel closes
- Prevent horizontal clipping or scrolling caused by the transition

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- When the panel is open, the main content occupies only the remaining space and no information is obscured
- When the panel is closed, the main content returns to its existing layout and width
- The main content remains fully visible and interactive while the panel is open
- Opening or closing the panel never causes horizontal clipping or makes content inaccessible

# Plan: Issue #68 — Audit sidebar layout & bring it into the shared layout flow

## Context
Issue #68 asks for an audit of how the side panel (the left `Sidebar`) and the main budget view are laid out, so that both share one layout context and the main content can react to whether the panel is open. Issue #69 builds on this to resize the main content. **Taking the floating sidebar out of `position: absolute` is deferred to #69**, because doing it here causes a regression. That leaves #68 as a small change: write up the audit, and give the layout one source of truth for the panel's state.

## Audit findings (go in the PR description)
- **Shared container already exists.** [FinancesApp.tsx:203-220](packages/desktop-client/src/components/FinancesApp.tsx#L203-L220) renders a `flexDirection: 'row'` `View`. Its children are `<FloatableSidebar />` and the main-content `View` (`flex: 1, overflow: 'hidden', width: '100%'`).
- **Docked mode** (`floatingSidebar` pref off and width ≥ 668): the wrapper in [sidebar/index.tsx](packages/desktop-client/src/components/sidebar/index.tsx) has no `position`. It sits in the flex row as a normal item, and its width comes from `Resizable` in [Sidebar.tsx](packages/desktop-client/src/components/sidebar/Sidebar.tsx) (200 to width/3, default 240). There is an odd offset (`bottom: -50` plus `translateY(-8px)`), but it only changes how the panel looks, not where it sits in the flow.
- **Floating mode** (pref on, or `alwaysFloats` when width < 668): the wrapper is `position: absolute` with `zIndex: 1001` and slides out using `translateX(-100%)` when `hidden`. This takes it out of the flow, so it sits on top of the main content. **This part is left for #69.**
- **Narrow width:** `FloatableSidebar` returns `null`, and mobile navigation takes over.
- **Panel state:** `SidebarProvider` ([SidebarProvider.tsx](packages/desktop-client/src/components/sidebar/SidebarProvider.tsx)) is mounted in [App.tsx:201](packages/desktop-client/src/components/App.tsx#L201), above `FinancesApp`. It already exposes `floating` and `hidden` through `useSidebar()`. However, `FloatableSidebar` doesn't use that `floating` value. It computes its own copy (`floatingSidebar || sidebar.alwaysFloats`) from the global pref, so the layout has two sources of truth.

## Code change (minimal)
In [sidebar/index.tsx](packages/desktop-client/src/components/sidebar/index.tsx):
- Remove the `useGlobalPref('floatingSidebar')` call and its import.
- Change it to `const sidebarShouldFloat = sidebar.floating;`. The provider computes exactly the same value (`floatingSidebar || alwaysFloats`), so behavior doesn't change. After this, the panel's position and anything #69 adds to `FinancesApp` read the same context state (`useSidebar().floating` / `.hidden`).
- Leave all styles exactly as they are (the `position: absolute` stays).

In [sidebar/index.test.tsx](packages/desktop-client/src/components/sidebar/index.test.tsx):
- Remove the `useGlobalPref` mock and its setup line, since the component no longer uses it. The `useSidebar` mock already passes `floating: floatingSidebar || alwaysFloats`, so all three existing tests still apply unchanged.

**Out of scope (leave untouched):** the main content's `width: '100%'` and any use of `useSidebar` in `FinancesApp` (both belong to #69). Also out of scope: the same duplicated `floatingSidebar || sidebar.alwaysFloats` in [Titlebar.tsx:298](packages/desktop-client/src/components/Titlebar.tsx#L298), and the docked `bottom: -50` offset.

## Verification
- `yarn workspace @actual-app/web run vitest --run src/components/sidebar` (or `yarn test`). The sidebar tests and `SidebarProvider.test.ts` must pass.
- `yarn typecheck` and `yarn lint:fix` from the repo root.
- Manual check with `yarn start` and View demo:
  - Docked: the sidebar sits beside the budget and resizing still works.
  - Toggle float: the panel hides, shows on hover, and still overlays as it does today.
  - Window < 668px wide: the panel always floats.
  - Narrow/mobile: no sidebar.
  - Navigation and budget pages work as before.
- PR title gets the `[AI]` prefix, the template stays unfilled, and the audit findings above go in a comment on the PR or the issue.

The new test doesn't actually protect anything: I broke the provider on purpose and all 10 tests still passed.

The only new commit since my last review is `c68cfb23b`, which adds the `alwaysFloats` test. The earlier commits are unchanged, so they still lack `[AI]`, and the new commit lacks it too.

## The new test can't fail

The test is at [index.test.tsx:63-72](packages/desktop-client/src/components/sidebar/index.test.tsx#L63-L72). Its `setup()` helper builds the mocked `useSidebar` like this:

```ts
floating: floatingSidebar || alwaysFloats,
```

So `setup({ floatingSidebar: false, alwaysFloats: true })` just hands the component `floating: true`. That's exactly what the existing "when floating" test already does. The OR it appears to test happens in the test helper, not in the app code.

To check this, I changed [SidebarProvider.tsx:39](packages/desktop-client/src/components/sidebar/SidebarProvider.tsx#L39) to `const floating = floatingSidebar;`, which drops `alwaysFloats` (a real regression), and ran the sidebar tests:

```
Test Files  2 passed (2)
     Tests  10 passed (10)
```

Then I reverted the change; the working tree is clean. **Nothing in the test suite checks how `floating` is computed.** That matters because this PR's whole point is making that value the one source of truth.

Smaller issues with the same test:
- **Misleading name.** "even if the floating pref is off" describes something `FloatableSidebar` can no longer see, since it doesn't read the pref after this PR.
- **Only half checked.** It tests `mouseOver` but not `mouseLeave`.

## Suggested fix

1. **Test the source of truth in [SidebarProvider.test.ts](packages/desktop-client/src/components/sidebar/SidebarProvider.test.ts).** It already mocks `useGlobalPref` and `useResponsive`, but fixes them at `false` and width `1000`, so `floating` is never checked:

   ```ts
   it.each([
     { pref: false, width: 1000, floating: false, alwaysFloats: false },
     { pref: true, width: 1000, floating: true, alwaysFloats: false },
     { pref: false, width: 600, floating: true, alwaysFloats: true },
     { pref: false, width: 668, floating: false, alwaysFloats: false },
   ])(
     'pref=$pref, width=$width → floating=$floating',
     ({ pref, width, floating, alwaysFloats }) => {
       (useGlobalPref as unknown as Mock).mockReturnValue([pref, vi.fn()]);
       (useResponsive as unknown as Mock).mockReturnValue({ width });
       const { result } = renderSidebar();
       expect(result.current.floating).toBe(floating);
       expect(result.current.alwaysFloats).toBe(alwaysFloats);
     },
   );
   ```

   The `width: 668` row checks the exact cutoff. That's the test that would have caught the change I made.

2. **Simplify [index.test.tsx](packages/desktop-client/src/components/sidebar/index.test.tsx).** Change `setup()` to take one `floating` option, matching what the component reads now. Then delete the new test, since it would just repeat the first one. With that change, `index.test.tsx` checks "floating → hover handlers attached" and `SidebarProvider.test.ts` checks "pref/width → floating". Each piece of logic is tested where it lives.
